# Justice The primary goal of the [color=#a4885c]Justice[/color] department is to uphold space law and process trials in a timely manner, handle sentencing and processing of prisoners, as well as enforce SOP and perform inspections.
## Roles - The [color=#a4885c]Chief Justice[/color] should act as a judge during hearings, prepare the department for upcoming trials, or review inspections. - The [color=#a4885c]Warden[/color] is in charge of all prisoners and securing all evidence. They should be aware of upcoming hearings and arrange prisoner transport. - [color=#a4885c]Attorneys[/color] should represent the defense during hearings, and should be contacting prisoners in need of defense or legal assistance. They also play a role as the public defender of the crew, also performing the function of [color=#a4885c]suing[/color] on behalf of the crew when needed. - [color=#a4885c]Prosecutors[/color] should represent (what else) the prosecution during hearings. In the case of an arrest, the Prosecutor should get a statement from the arresting officer about the matter, and is [color=#a4885c]responsible for sentencing[/color]. If available, the prosecutor should work with [color=#a4885c]detectives[/color] to request evidence. - [color=#a4885c]Marshals[/color] are the "muscle" of justice, and may act as prison guards, baliffs, or assist in performing inspections.
In the event of a trial being needed when [color=#a4885c]one of these roles is unavailable[/color]: - A substitute judge should be a member of the Justice department, or less preferably a member of Command or Security. - A substitute prosecutor should be either an attorney or clerk. - A substitute defense should be either a prosecutor or clerk, however the defendant has the right to represent themselves if they choose.
## Hearing Procedure All hearings should follow the [textlink="Hearing Procedure" link="HearingProcedure"]. It states how long a trial should last, and lists the steps on how it should be carried out.
It is reccomended to have a baliff during a court hearing, in order to escort prisoners and enforce order.
